Create GitHub issue for staff review * * * ##### Abstract Retrieval-based language models (LMs) have shown impressive performance on diverse NLP tasks. In this tutorial, we will provide a comprehensive and coherent overview of recent advances in retrieval-based LMs. We will start by providing preliminaries covering the foundation of LMs (e.g., masked LMs, autoregressive LMs) and retrieval systems (e.g., nearest-neighbor search). We will then detail recent progress in retrieval-based models, focusing on their model architectures and learning approaches. Finally, we will show how retrieval-based LMs are adapted to downstream applications, and extended to multilingual and multi-modal settings. Finally, we will use an exercise to showcase the effectiveness of retrieval-based LMs. Anthology ID: 2023.acl-tutorials.6 Volume: Proceedings of the 61st Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 6: Tutorial Abstracts)⟨30⟩ Month: July Year: 2023 Address: Toronto, Canada Editors: Yun-Nung (Vivian) Chen⟨31⟩, Margot Mieskes⟨32⟩, Siva Reddy⟨33⟩ Venue: ACL⟨34⟩ SIG: Publisher: Association for Computational Linguistics Note: Pages: 41–46 Language: URL: DOI: 10.18653/v1/2023.acl-tutorials.6⟨35⟩ Bibkey: asai-etal-2023-retrieval Cite (ACL): Akari Asai, Sewon Min, Zexuan Zhong, and Danqi Chen. 2023.
